# Caixin Global — In Depth: Chinese Tech Giants' Struggle to Power AI Data Center Boom

By Zhao Xuan, Qin Min, Fan Ruohong, Wang Xintong. Published May 16, 2025. (Article partially paywalled; key figures recovered from the free "Digest Hub" summary.)

## Key figures
- In 2024, Chinese data centers consumed around 140 billion kWh of electricity, up 31% year-on-year, far exceeding the national total power consumption growth of 6.8%.
- CAICT projection: 400 billion kWh by 2030, raising data centers' share of national electricity use from less than 2% to 6%.
- Intelligent computing centers ("AI brain factories") require 20–130 kW per server cabinet vs. 5–10 kW in traditional cloud data centers.
- Intelligent computing sector projected to grow 33.9% annually from 2022 to 2027 (IDC).
- 2022 initiative channels computing from the east (renewables <40% of supply) to the west, which holds 70% of installed renewable capacity.
- Tencent's Huailai (Hebei) microgrid project (wind + solar + battery storage) meets just 15% of annual electricity demand; the bulk still from the state grid at higher prices.
- Rooftop solar can usually provide less than 5% of a data center's electricity needs (vs. 20–30% possible in manufacturing plants).
- Western/northern regions offer subsidized electricity as low as 0.35–0.36 yuan/kWh vs. over 0.6 yuan elsewhere.
- Qingyang (Gansu): every yuan spent on computing generates 3–4 yuan in local output; local digital economy expected to surpass 100 billion yuan in 2024.
- Inner Mongolia revoked electricity subsidies in 2022 to comply with central directives.
- Tencent aims to use 100% renewable electricity in its data centers by 2030.
- National computing hubs in Ningxia attract Tencent, Baidu, and the major telecom providers (China Mobile, China Telecom, China Unicom).
